data.short_meaning: Derived from Silvester, from silva (latin for forest).
data.long_meaning: The name Sylwester is derived from the Latin name Silvester, which was originally a Roman family name. The name is composed of the elements silva, meaning forest, and ster, meaning man or ruler. The name Silvester was originally given to children born on the feast day of Saint Silvester, which is celebrated on December 31st. In Christian legend, Saint Silvester was a pope who ruled during the late 3rd or early 4th century. He is traditionally believed to have presided over the baptism of the Roman Emperor Constantine I, who is considered the first Christian Roman Emperor.
